rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although eyd could be the plural of yad, here it plainly means strength, as in the description of David.
rows.anchor: “Eyd” “yed”in cem‘i olabilirse de burada

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's vastness means either inexhaustible power, able to enlarge the heavens, or abundant generosity that relieves hardship and enriches the poor.
rows.anchor: Bunda iki mâna vardır: Birisi kudret genişliğini ifade eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God spread the earth like a bed, adorning it with blessings so people can dwell there and enjoy life for a time; He can provide still better blessings later.
rows.anchor: Arz, onu da döşedik -türlü nimetlerle donattık

rows.speaker: İbn Zeyd
rows.claim: He interprets pairs as male and female members of each animal kind, a reading that can include plants as well.
rows.anchor: İbn Zeyd gibi bazı zatlar[^2] bunu her cins hayvandan erkek

rows.speaker: Mücâhid
rows.claim: He takes pairs to indicate opposites such as motion and rest, night and day, health and illness, pleasure and pain, and reward and punishment.
rows.anchor: Mücâhid hareket ve sükûn, leyl ü nehar, semâ ve Arz

rows.speaker: Beyzâvî
rows.claim: He interprets pairs as two kinds within genera; the author says this broad reading can include earlier interpretations, though it narrows all things to genera.
rows.anchor: Beyzâvî yalnız bu mânayı göstererek مِنَ الأَْجْنَاسِ نـَوْعَيْنِ diye tefsir etmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording's apparent universality also points to each thing's outward and inward, external and mental forms, whose correspondence makes knowledge and judgment possible.
rows.anchor: her şeyin âfâkī ve enfüsî yahut hâricî ve zihnî olmak üzere iki haysiyetini ifade eden

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The created-pair wording excludes God: He is unlike anything, uncreated, and does not depend on a mental image or a counterpart for knowledge of Himself.
rows.anchor: buradaki كُلِّ شَىْءٍ خَلَقْنَا karînesiyle ancak mahlûkāta şâmil olabilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı rejects Ibn Arabi's proposed inclusion of God among the pairs, arguing that God is not included in the phrase just as He is excluded from the created-things phrase.
rows.anchor: Muhyiddîn-i Arabî’nin buradaki كُلِّ شَىْءٍ’de O’nu dahi idhal eder yollu mütalaada bulunması doğru değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Created pairs invite reflection on God's power, wisdom, severe punishment, abundant favor, and the relations between this world and the next, including their recompense.
rows.anchor: çiftler arasındaki münâsebâtı düşünesiniz de yaratanın kuvvet ve kudretini, sun‘unun hikmetini,

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People should flee to God's protection through faith, oneness, excellence, and worship, seeking safety from punishment and entry among the God-fearing promised gardens and springs.
rows.anchor: îmân ü tevhid ve ihsân u ubûdiyet ile O’nun vikāyesine girin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is a clear warner commissioned to announce punishment for idolatry and disobedience; his prophethood is evident through signs and miracles, and he explains what must be explained well.
rows.anchor: peygamberliği açık âyât ve mu‘cizât ile belli, yahut anlatılması lâzım gelen şeyleri güzel anlatır bir peygamberim

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition against taking another god alongside God separately warns against the greatest sin from which people must flee first.
rows.anchor: Bu nehiy, ilk evvel kaçılması lâzım gelen en büyük günahı ayrıca ihtardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that earlier peoples called messengers sorcerers or madmen consoles the Prophet by showing that his opponents repeat an old pattern.
rows.anchor: bu âyet Resûlullah’a bir tesliyedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rhetorical question denies that distant peoples coordinated their insults; their shared accusations instead arise because all are transgressive and speak alike in defiance of truth.
rows.anchor: diyenler hep {قَوْمٌۭ طَاغُونَ} tuğyan etmiş azgınlar gürûhudur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question whether they advised one another is rhetorical: many had no knowledge of one another, yet their transgression made their accusations alike.
rows.anchor: çoklarının birbirlerinden haberleri bile yok

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After repeating the summons and completing his duty, the Prophet may turn away from those who persist in stubborn transgression instead of continuing disputes.
rows.anchor: Onun için sen şimdi onlardan yüz çevir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is not blameworthy for turning away from them after fulfilling his duty.
rows.anchor: O surette levm olunacak, kınanacak sen değilsin, sende kusur olmaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet must continue reminding people because it benefits believers by renewing memory and faith, preventing heedlessness, increasing joy, teaching the uninformed, and sometimes bringing people to faith.
rows.anchor: İman etmiş olanların unutmamasına, gaflete düşmemesine, imanlarının kuvvetlenmesine

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The essential reminder is that jinn and humans were created to know God and worship Him; lives spent on other ends are wasted and merit punishment.
rows.anchor: Cin ve ins cinsinin hilkatlerinin hikmeti Allah’ı tanıyıp O’na ibadet ve ubûdiyet etmektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some interpret the purpose as knowing God; Elmalılı says this amounts to recognizing Him as worthy of worship and obeying His commands.
rows.anchor: Bazıları لِيـَعْرِفُونَ,لِيَعْبُدُونِ diye bir tefsir nakletmişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse means humans were created with the duty of worship, not that every individual was decreed to become righteous; divine wisdom is considered at the level of the species.
rows.anchor: hikmet, efrâdın her biri itibariyle değil, cins itibariyle mülâhaza olunur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God seeks neither provision nor food from creatures; unlike masters who expect service for their own benefit, worship benefits the servants.
rows.anchor: Ben onlardan bir rızık istemem, Bana yemek yedirmelerini de istemem

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone is the Provider, mighty and strong; worship lets servants benefit from His power and attain the high reward He promises.
rows.anchor: Metîn, yani kuvveti şiddetli. Onun için O’na kulluk O’nun kuvvetinden istifade

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who wrong themselves by rejecting the Prophet and fleeing worship through idolatry and rebellion, like Meccan polytheists, have a full share of punishment like their predecessors.
rows.anchor: şirk ü tuğyan ile kendilerini ebedî azâba sürükleyerek nefislerine yazık etmiş olan Mekke müşrikleri gibilere

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zenub originally denotes a full large bucket used in distributing water; here it is metaphorical for a full share of punishment.
rows.anchor: sakaların su taksim ettikleri dolgun büyük

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelievers should stop demanding that the promised punishment arrive quickly; the question echoes their challenge in Jonah 10:48.
rows.anchor: Şimdi onu Benden acele istemesinler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Woe awaits disbelievers on the day promised to them; its certainty was stated at the beginning of this surah and is reinforced by the next surah, At-Tur.
rows.anchor: zira sûrenin başında geçtiği üzere إِنَّمَا تُوعَدُونَ لَصَادِقٌۭ وَإِنَّ ٱلدِّينَ لَوَٰقِعٌۭ’dir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the Turkish rendering, Elmalılı describes the heaven as beautiful and says God gave it elevation while placing the balance.
rows.anchor: verdi ona irtifâ‘vaz‘eyleyip mîzânı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He renders the command as keeping the weighing straight with justice and not diminishing the balance.
rows.anchor: doğru tutun adaletle tartıyı da aksatmayın mîzânı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rahman names God as the one whose mercy and beneficence are boundless and continually joined; Elmalılı refers readers to his earlier explanation in the Fatiha commentary.
rows.anchor: nâmütenâhî kaynaşıp duran ve ondan dolayı bir ismi de Rahmân olan Allah teâlâ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although Rahman appears grammatically as a subject followed by its predicate, its status as a separate verse permits reading it as the predicate of an omitted subject: God is Rahman.
rows.anchor: İ‘rabca zâhir olan mübtedâ, mâba‘di haber görünür. Lâkin müstakil bir âyet

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because teaching takes two objects, the first is omitted here; this presents teaching the Quran itself and leaves its recipients open to Gabriel, the Prophet, and the community.
rows.anchor: bu mânaca burada birinci mef‘ul hazfedilmiş ve bu suretle maksad şuna veya buna ta‘lîmi değil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some read allama as making the Quran a sign or prophetic miracle, which needs no omitted object and parallels the preceding surah's opening miracle of the moon's splitting.
rows.anchor: Bazıları da demişler ki burada عَلَّمَ alâmettendir; “Kur’ân’ı alâmet kıldı”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı favors translating the verb as ta‘lim etti, since that Turkish wording preserves both the teaching and sign interpretations.
rows.anchor: tâlim etti” denilirse bu iki veche de işaret mahfuz kalmış olur

rows.speaker: Âlûsî
rows.claim: Even if a connection to signs is proposed, the verse must still be understood as teaching Quranic knowledge, including its words and meanings, with levels of insight extending to cosmic events.
rows.anchor: Kāil bin münasebet de gösterse yine bunun ilim tâliminden olduğu bilinmek gerektir

rows.speaker: İbn Mes‘ûd
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Masud says the Quran contains knowledge concerning everything and explains everything, though human knowledge cannot encompass it all.
rows.anchor: Kur’an’da her şeye dair ilim indirilmiş ve her şey beyan edilmiş ise de bizim ilmimiz onun hepsine yetişemez

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says that even if his camel's rope went missing, he would find it in God's Book.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas da demiştir ki: ‘Devemin bir ipi kaybolsa

rows.speaker: Mürsî
rows.claim: Mursi says the Quran gathers the sciences of earlier and later peoples, but its full reality is known only to God; interpretive knowledge passes from God to the Prophet, leading Companions, and their Successor heirs, except what God reserves.
rows.anchor: Mürsî demiş[^7] ki: ‘Kur’an evvelîn ve âhirînin ulûmunu câmi‘dir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some define teaching as awakening the mind to conceive meanings.
rows.anchor: Bazıları ‘ta‘lîm’i; tasavvur-ı me‘ânî için nefsi tenbih diye târif etmişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As the Hour approaches, teaching the Quran is presented as the greatest and most important blessing arising from divine mercy.
rows.anchor: en büyük ve en mühim nimetin ta‘lîm-i Kur’an nimeti olduğu bu suretle anlatıldıktan sonra

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some take the human as Adam, and others as Muhammad because of the Quran context; Elmalılı prefers humankind generally, while allowing the perfect human as the Quran's recipient.
rows.anchor: hepsine şâmil olmak üzere cins-i insan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bayan is the gift of articulate language: expressing oneself, feelings, perceptions, and will clearly to others, and understanding them; Quranic knowledge and teaching also depend on it.
rows.anchor: kendini ve vicdan ve zamîrindeki duygu ve idrâkât ve irâdâtını

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam learned what angels did not through the names; prophets' revelation and communication, communities' benefit from scripture, and people's access to Quran and its interpretation depend on the gift of bayan.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Âdem yaradıldıktan sonra ta‘lîm-i esmâ sayesinde melâikenin bilemediklerini bildi

rows.speaker: Ebussuud
rows.claim: Abu Suud says teaching bayan includes understanding another person's expression, not merely being able to express oneself, since Quran teaching depends on it; the successive clauses are synonymous and omit conjunction as enumeration.
rows.anchor: Beyânı ta‘lîmden murad, insanı mücerred kendi beyânına temkinden ibaret değil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting the subject in the construction conveys restriction.
rows.anchor: Müsned-i ileyhin takdîmi de kasr ifade eyler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun and moon run according to calculation; people should learn calculation and prepare for the coming day of reckoning.
rows.anchor: Hesab ile cereyan ederler. Binâen‘aleyh insanlar hesabı iyi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Husban can mean calculation, the plural of calculation, or the axle of a millstone.
rows.anchor: “Hüsbân” “hâ”nın zammıyla hesab mânasına ve “hesab”ın cem‘i hesablar mânasına gelir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Najm is a ground-growing plant without a stem, while shajar is a stemmed plant; both prostrate by obeying God's will and adapting to His natural laws, so people should willingly obey and prostrate in gratitude.
rows.anchor: necim yani Arz’dan zuhur edip de sâkı olmayan nebat, çimen

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The syntax first suppresses the object of raised and then resumes it with a pronoun, foregrounding heaven and specifically emphasizing the act of raising it.
rows.anchor: kelâm, وَرَفَعَ ال َّسمَاءَ رَفـَعَهَا takdîrindedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Heaven means the encompassing cosmos and its celestial bodies; its elevation is its high creation, chiefly physical though also open to a figurative spiritual sense.
rows.anchor: “Semâ”dan murad, bütün ecrâmıyla üzerimizde yükselen muhît-i âlemdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The visible height of heaven shows the greatness of the Rahman's creative mercy and His exaltedness above directions and place, making Him worthy of prostration and reverence.
rows.anchor: semânın böyle rif‘ati onu yükselten Rahmân’ın sun‘u rahmetinin yüksekliğini

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The balance is the law of equilibrium and justice that gives each thing its due place among masses, beings, and rights; without it the heavens and earth could not remain ordered.
rows.anchor: aşağı ve yukarı muhtelif ve müte‘addid sıkletler, mevcûdiyetler, hukuklar arasında her şeyin hakkına göre

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith states that the heavens and earth stand through justice.
rows.anchor: بِالْعَدْلِ قَامَتِ ال َّسموَاتُ وَالأَْرْضُ buyurulmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mizan can be the verbal noun weighing or the instrument scales; weighing compares quantities, so the term also denotes justice and its standard, the Sharia, or any measuring instrument.
rows.anchor: “Mîzân” “mîsâk” gibi hem vezin mânasına masdar, hem de vezin âleti terazi mânasına ism-i âlet olabilir

rows.speaker: Zemahşerî
rows.claim: Zamakhshari reads the three mentions of mizan as emphatic repetition to reinforce the admonition.
rows.anchor: sâhib-Keşşâf bunun tavsiyeyi teşdid ve takviye için bir tekrar olduğunu söylemiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı rejects a single repeated meaning for all three mentions, arguing that three successive endings are unlikely to repeat one sense and that each signals a distinct sense.
rows.anchor: üç fâsılanın aynı mânada bir tekrardan ibaret olması pek muvâfık olamayacağı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first mizan is the universal equilibrium law, most visibly gravity, underlying scales and weights and operating throughout celestial and terrestrial bodies; in a wider reading it also covers chemical and spiritual relations as justice.
rows.anchor: bütün eşya arasındaki muvâzene-i umûmiye kanunudur

rows.speaker: Beyzâvî
rows.claim: Baydawi defines justice as ordering worldly affairs by giving each capable thing what it deserves and each rights-holder the right due to them.
rows.anchor: her müsta‘idde müstehakkını, her sâhib-i hakka hakkını vermek suretiyle umûr-ı âlemin intizam ve istikāmeti

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second mizan is the verbal noun or the Sharia, and the third is the scale of deeds in the afterlife, though other allocations are possible.
rows.anchor: ikinci “mîzân” masdar yahut şeriat, üçüncüsü de âhiretteki mîzân-ı a‘mâl olmak gerektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command not to transgress the balance means not to exceed the Sharia or law, act without measure, or overreach in material and spiritual weighing; people must obey God's rulings and respect rights.
rows.anchor: şeriat ve kanuna tecavüz edip de haddinizi aşmayasınız

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People must weigh words and deeds fairly, use full measures, and judge with the same standard for themselves and others; they must not misuse the scales or ruin their afterlife scale.
rows.anchor: hem vezni, kavil ve fiil her hususta tartmak işini adaletle doğru tutun

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Haqqa is undisputedly one of the names of the Resurrection, like al-Waqia and al-Saa, but commentators offer more than ten explanations of its relation to truth and realization.
rows.anchor: “el- Hâkka”; “el-Vâkı‘a”, “es-Sâ‘a” gibi kıyamet gününün isimlerinden olduğunda ihtilâf yoktur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation derives it from truth as something fixed and obligatory: the Hour whose arrival is certain and inevitable.
rows.anchor: “Hak” sâbit ve vâcib mânasına olarak “el-Hâkka” vukū‘u vâcib

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation makes it the Hour when matters are recognized in their true reality and things are disclosed.
rows.anchor: kendisinde umûr hakikatiyle tanınacak, yani eşyânın hakikatini keşf ü izhar edecek Sâ‘at

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further interpretation calls it the event containing affairs whose truth and occurrence are certain, such as reward and punishment.
rows.anchor: havâkk-ı umûru hâvî, yani kendisinde sıdk u tahakkuku vâcib sâbit umûr ve ahvâl vâki‘olan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another gloss relates haqqa to a person's special, particular right, using the expression 'this is my own right.'
rows.anchor: “Hâkka”, “hakka” mânasınadır. “Hakka”, “hukūk”un müfredi olan “hak”tan ehastır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is an unfailing calamity that comes and carries out what it will, as in the description that its occurrence has no lie.
rows.anchor: şaşmaksızın inen ve yapacağını yalansız yapan musibet demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It can also mean the appointed time whose occurrence has become due upon a people, close to the sense of an inevitable Hour.
rows.anchor: Kavim üzerine vukū‘u hak olan vakit demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may refer to the time when every doer receives the true recompense for good or evil and every deed is requited.
rows.anchor: her âmile amelinin hak olduğu vakit demektir ki o kıyamettir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is the Hour when all effects of people's deeds become fully realized and rewards and punishments come to pass.
rows.anchor: Mükellefînin amellerinin hepsinin âsârı tamamıyla tahakkuk edip intizar haddinden çıktığı hak Sâ‘at

rows.speaker: Ezherî
rows.claim: Al-Haqqa can derive from overcoming in a contest: God overcomes those who challenge His religion with falsehood.
rows.anchor: Ezherî’nin kavlince muhasama ve mügālebe mânasına حَاققته فحققته

rows.speaker: Ebû Müslim
rows.claim: Abu Muslim derives the active form from the phrase that the word of the Lord has come true.
rows.anchor: Ebû Müslim’in kavlince “el-Hâkka”, حَقَّتْ كَلِمَتُ رَبِّكَ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another analysis treats it as an abstract verbal noun like aqiba or afiya, meaning pure reality itself.
rows.anchor: “Âkıbet”, “âfiyet” gibi masdardır ki mahz-ı hakikat demek olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A final view treats al-Haqqa simply as a proper name of Resurrection without any further intended meaning.
rows.anchor: Kıyametin ismi olması itibariyle başkaca mefhum melhuz olmayarak ism-i câmiddir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The many proposed nuances notwithstanding, the following question indicates that the Haqqa is not something one can know through unaided reasoning.
rows.anchor: “el-Hâkka” وَمَآ أَدْرَىٰكَ مَا ٱلْحَآقَّةُ buyurulduğu üzere dirayetle bilinir bir şey değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question 'What is the Haqqa?' magnifies the terror and enormity of the event, and the next question intensifies that dread.
rows.anchor: bu istifham i‘zâm ve tehvil içindir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammatically, the first ma is an interrogative subject, adra-ka is its predicate, the addressed pronoun is the first object, and the question what the Haqqa is forms the second object.
rows.anchor: “Mâ” yine istifham için mübtedâ, “dirâyet”ten أَدْرَىٰكَ fiili haber

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No created being can comprehend the Haqqa's severity by estimation; its actual occurrence will disclose it, while beforehand it is known only through divine report and faith in that report cannot fully encompass its reality.
rows.anchor: onun şiddet ve fezâ‘atinin azameti mahlûkāttan birinin dirayetiyle, tahmin ve takdîri ile bilinemez

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who disbelieve the transmitted report because reason cannot grasp the event dismiss it as superstition, fable, poetry, invention, or deception.
rows.anchor: evhâm, masal, hurafe, şiir, uydurma, aldatma diye türlü laflarla tekzîbe kalkışırlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A powerful admonition points to past catastrophes, whose terrifying outcomes became proverbial, to make people sense some of the dangers awaiting the future.
rows.anchor: geçmiş vak‘aların ihbar ve ihtârıyla istikbâlin namzed olduğu tehlikeleri bir dereceye kadar olsun sezdirmektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The peoples of Thamud and Ad denied the coming Qaria; the name means a striking event and refers to Resurrection, with the surah's imagery of scattered people and carded mountains, foreshadowed in their destruction.
rows.anchor: Kāri‘a” lügatta insanların başlarına çarpan, beyinlerinde patlayan vak‘a demek olup

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taghiya means a transgressing event or tyranny; Thamud's was the blast described elsewhere as a cry, a thunderous blast, and the earthquake that accompanied it.
rows.anchor: “Tâğiye” tuğyan eden, haddini aşan vâkı‘a, tağvâ gibi tuğyan mânasına da gelir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common Turkish 'vay hâline' fails to convey wail's severity and gives no hint of the report that it is a proper name; 'veyl ona' or 'vâveyla' better reflects its established Turkish usage.
rows.anchor: bizim “vay” tâbiri Arabın “veyh” kelimesine mukabil olduğundan veylin şiddetini pek duyurmadığı gibi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wail has been explained as severe evil, grief and destruction, painful punishment, or a valley in Hell.
rows.anchor: hüzn ü helâk, azâb-ı elîm, cehennemde bir vâdi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Prophetic report from Abu Said says Wail is a valley in Hell where a disbeliever falls for forty years before reaching its bottom.
rows.anchor: Veyl cehennemde bir vâdidir ki kâfir, ka‘rına varmadan evvel onda kırk yıl sukūt eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports in Ibn Hibban's and Hakim's Sahih collections describe Wail as a valley between two mountains in Hell.
rows.anchor: İbn Hibbân’ın ve Hâkim’in Sahîhlerinde: “Cebeleyn beyninde bir vadidir

rows.speaker: Abdullah
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Hatim transmits from Abdullah that Wail is a valley of pus in Hell.
rows.anchor: İbn Ebî Hâtim de Abdullah’tan “Cehennemde irinden bir vâdidir” diye rivayet etmiştir

rows.speaker: Asma‘î
rows.claim: Asmai says wail means something vile or ugly and can also express regret; those calling it a valley mean that its condemned recipients deserve a place in the fire, not that valley is its lexical meaning.
rows.anchor: “‘Veyl’ bir kubuh, yani bir çirkinliktir. Bazen tehassür için de kullanılır

rows.speaker: Âlûsî
rows.claim: Alusi says applying wail to the recognized sense of Hell appears to be a kind of figurative transfer, though its precise type should be examined.
rows.anchor: Ona veyl ıtlak edilmesi cehennemin mâruf olan mânasına ıtlâkı gibi olmak zâhirdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı considers Hell's conventional sense an established religious usage also absorbed into ordinary language, whereas Wail as a particular valley is an unestablished religious metaphor, not common lexicon; 'vay hâline' therefore only partly translates it.
rows.anchor: “veyl”in îzah olunan mâna ile cehennemde bir vâdi ismi olması şer‘î bir ıtlak olmakla beraber mütevâtir olmadığı gibi lügaten de müte‘âref olmayan bir mecaz olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mutaffifin is the plural of mutaffif: those who take full measure but give less, as the following two verses clarify; Turkish has no exact independent equivalent.
rows.anchor: mutaffifler, alırken dolgun, verirken eksik ölçenler demek olduğu önünde sıfat-ı kâşife olan iki âyet ile anlatılmıştır

rows.speaker: Râzî
rows.claim: Razi's first etymology connects tatfif to the edge of a vessel: something reaching its rim without filling it, so the mutaffif gives an incomplete measure.
rows.anchor: Bir şeyin taffi, kıyısı ve kenarıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lexicon also uses taff and related forms for a filled measure, its leveled remainder, or its top; on this account tatfif subtracts from the proper measure.
rows.anchor: “Taff”, “tafef”, “tafâf”, “tufâf” bir ölçeği veya kabı tam dolduran şeye

rows.speaker: Râzî
rows.claim: Razi's second etymology derives it from a tiny amount: a mutaffif steals a little in measuring or weighing, and the habitual form suits the verse better.
rows.anchor: Pek az bir şeye ‘tafîf’ denilir, ölçeği eksik ölçene ‘mutaffif’ denilmesi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı finds the second derivation more consistent with the verse's description of the mutaffifin.
rows.anchor: Bu vecih âyetteki tefsire daha mutâbıktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording says buyers take full measure for themselves against people; using 'against' rather than 'from' signals acting to people's detriment, asserting power and insisting on full value.
rows.anchor: Burada ifadenin zâhiri مِنَ النَّاس “nâstan” denilmekti, عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ buyurulması kendi lehlerine olarak nâsın aleyhine istîlâ ve tecavüz suretiyle ölçtüklerine işaret içindir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When measuring or weighing for those same people, they reduce the amount or otherwise shortchange them; habitual fraud explains their deserving Wail.
rows.anchor: eksiltirler eksik ölçek veya tartı ile ölçerler veya ölçüşte, tartışta eksik yapar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If those who steal a little merit Wail, people who steal much more deserve to fear it even more.
rows.anchor: Böyle az bir şey çalanlar veyle müstahik olursa çok çalanların kaç katlı veyle müstahik olacakları düşünülmeli

rows.speaker: Râzî
rows.claim: Razi recounts an Arab telling Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan that if tiny cheats receive this warning, the ruler who takes Muslims' wealth in vast amounts should consider his fate.
rows.anchor: sen ise çoğu alıyorsun, müslimînin emvâlini ölçüsüz tartısız alıyorsun

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning weighing as well as measuring shows that the initial mention of measure is shorthand, not a restriction: tatfif can occur with every kind of quantity measure.
rows.anchor: Burada veznin de söylenmesi evvelkinde yalnız keylin zikri tahsis için değil, iktifâ kabîlinden olduğunu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the heavens and earth stand through balance and justice, and the balance measures all rights, social justice first requires accurate, equal measures for everyone.
rows.anchor: Sûre-i Rahmân’da ve Sûre-i Hadîd’de dahi geçtiği üzere mâlumdur ki semâvât ve Arz’ın kıvâmı muvâzene ve adalet iledir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fair measuring requires both complete, accurate instruments and honest, just use; the latter depends especially on fairness and uprightness of spirit.
rows.anchor: Bunun doğru olması için iki rükün lâzımdır. Birisi: ölçünün haddizâtında tam olması

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People lacking justice, uprightness, and faith may cheat even with accurate equipment; equal concern for others' rights and one's own is necessary to avoid tatfif.
rows.anchor: Kalb ve vicdanlarında insaf ve istikāmetle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person may treat losing a tiny amount as painful for themselves but dismiss or enjoy the same loss for another; this is tatfif in the inner scale of judgment.
rows.anchor: kendinin bir habbesi zâyi‘olmasını bir elem saydıkları hâlde başkasının bir habbesi zâyi‘olmasına

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This inward bias drives physical fraud: even accurate scales will be misused whenever those with such a disposition find an opportunity.
rows.anchor: Asıl bu hâlet-i rûhiyedir ki kilede terazide tatfîfe sâik olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All such people fall under the name mutaffifin and deserve Wail; correcting measures is a first step toward ordering rights and establishing virtue.
rows.anchor: Bunların hepsi “mutaffifîn” unvânında dâhil ve veyle müstahiktirler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The underlying cause is a defective belief that neglects the afterlife and accountability, so reform must begin by reviving faith in resurrection and responsibility.
rows.anchor: bunun asıl sebebi hak ve âhiret düşüncesini ihmal ettiren itikad bozukluğu olduğu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even those who reject resurrection should at least consider it possible; mere belief that they will be raised for the great day should deter them from cheating.
rows.anchor: iman etmiyorlarsa bir zan da mı beslemezler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that day people rise from their graves and stand before God for judgment, where the wronged receive their rights from wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: O gün herkes kabirlerinden uyanıp kalkarak Allah için kıyam edecek, O’nun huzûrunda muhakemeye durup haklı haksızdan hakkını alacaktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kalla is a rebuke and warning meant to make people stop cheating and heedlessness about resurrection: no, desist and beware.
rows.anchor: “Hayır hayır yapmayın, sakının” demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The record of the wicked is certainly in Sijjin: their register and deeds are inscribed there as the document of judgment and punishment they will receive at resurrection.
rows.anchor: fâcirler ise “siccîn” denilen sicilde mukayyeddirler; onların yazısı: nüfus kayıdları, amel defterleri

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sijjin may mean prison or confinement, something lasting and severe, the place where the wicked's book is kept, or a ravine in Hell; lexicons also record public or date-palm senses.
rows.anchor: dâim ve şedîd ve füccâr kitabının mevzi‘i ve cehennemde bir dere mânalarına
